ety.text: Borrowed from North Caucasian languages, specifically West Circassian абрэгь (abrɛgʲ) (standart Adyghe абрэдж (abrɛdž)). The term is widely distributed across the Caucasus; compare Ossetian абырӕг (abyræg), Chechen обург (oburg), Georgian აბრაგი (abragi). Compare Armenian ավազակ (avazak, “robber”). V.I. Abaev suggests the ultimate origin is Middle Persian *āparak (“robber”), related to āpartan (“to rob”) and āpar (“robbery”). This implies a connection to Persian آواره (âvâre, “vagabond, wanderer”).
